additional_concerns: Nodes node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 convert preserved application processing into a relief exclusion. That is a proposed interpretation, not an expressly established substantive disqualification. Its duration and treatment of subsequent decisions, withdrawal or resubmission remain unresolved.

Node node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from scope; it does not decide their eligibility. Node node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa tests substantive conditions only; a true result does not establish actual procedural relief.
Node node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 supplies no executable meaning. Its unresolved actual-relief question cannot produce an executable eligibility determination.

The introductory immediate-effect wording and specific 28 November 2025 implementation provision must be read together. The latter supports commencement, but does not establish a universal implementation-date test or settle every relevant assessment event.

The updated FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds, relevant related FAQs and existing approval or authorisation rules are missing for resolving procedural availability and transition. Neither supplied opaque dependency ID can safely be mapped to a named authority; both have null source_hash values.

Concrete classification requires applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and any relevant authoritative guidance on novelty, complexity and local policy implications. The formulas accept these classifications as inputs rather than determining them.

The home-supervision aim is supported as context. Whether it also limits broader relief availability remains unresolved; item (ii) does not expressly impose a separate supervision test. Item (i)'s express supervision condition cannot automatically be imported.
These scoped assessments neither establish a complete approval obligation nor authorize pruning supported contextual or enforcement claims.
